In the time before time, when the sky was an endless void, there lived a lonely weaver named Celeste. She dwelt in a cottage at the edge of the world, where earth met emptiness.

Each night, Celeste gazed into the darkness and wept, for the world felt cold and forsaken. Her tears fell upward into the void, freezing as they rose. One tear, the purest of all, transformed into a brilliant point of light—the first star.

The people below noticed the growing lights and felt less alone. They began to tell stories about the patterns they saw—a hunter, a bear, a swan. Their stories gave the stars meaning, and their meaning gave the stars strength to shine brighter.

Celeste still weaves today, though no one remembers her name. When a star falls, it is merely a thread come loose. When a new star appears, it is Celeste, still working through the endless night, ensuring that no one ever feels as alone as she once did.

**The Weaver of Dawn**

In the time before time, darkness covered the world like a heavy blanket. The people huddled in caves, knowing only cold and shadow.

High in the mountains lived an old woman whom no one had seen. Each night, she sat at her loom, weaving threads of gold and crimson, orange and pink. Her fingers moved ceaselessly, pulling light from the stars themselves.

One brave child climbed the mountain to find her. "Grandmother," the child asked, "why do you weave in darkness?"

The woman smiled. "I do not weave in darkness, little one. I weave *against* it."

She showed the child her tapestry—a magnificent cloth that shimmered with every color of fire. "Each thread is a promise," she explained. "When my work is complete, I cast it across the sky."

"What happens then?" asked the child.

"Watch."

The old woman flung her tapestry eastward. It unfurled across the horizon, blazing brilliant. The darkness retreated. Warmth spread across the land.

"This is dawn," she said. "But night always returns, so I must weave again."

And so she does, every night, weaving the sunrise that chases away the dark—a gift that must be remade each day.

Thus began the eternal dance of day and night—two gifts, forever alternating, neither complete without the other.
